assertions.name: transforms_scored
assertions.source: Hypothesis plus every null control scored identically.

assertions.name: alpha_monotone_within_2pct
assertions.source: H_coth requires the implied pair separation to grow with A; tested to a 2% tolerance on the A=11 wobble.

description: EXPLORATORY geometry-first test of the open two-like-charge EM-linking invariant (bean qou-zp6a). Hypothesis H_coth: the missing per-pair factor is the H^3 Coulomb kernel at the pair separation, kappa(A) = coth(alpha(A)). Inverts the existing kappa(A) data (NO fitting; coth is forced by the Green's function) and tests the implied separations against the independent nuclear-radius expectation alpha ~ A^(1/3), scored against NULL compressive transforms to control for the automatic variance reduction of arccoth. Nothing wired; four data points is a direction indicator, not evidence.

monotonicity.note: A monotone-increasing alpha(A) is REQUIRED by H_coth, since coth is decreasing: kappa falls with A only if the pair separation grows with A.

discrimination.why: arccoth(k) = 1/k + 1/(3k^3) + ... , so on the observed range k in [2.1, 3.2] the two transforms agree to a few percent. The A <= 13 data therefore CANNOT select the hyperbolic kernel over a generic reciprocal law.
discrimination.discriminating_test: The two hypotheses diverge at large A and in OPPOSITE directions: H_coth has kappa -> 1 (the derived per-pair unit becomes correct in heavy nuclei), while the 1/kappa power law has kappa -> 0 (the derived unit overshoots). Extending the kappa(A) mirror-pair table to A ~ 27-57 separates them decisively and requires no new theory, only more AME mirror pairs.

data.saturation_prediction: coth(alpha) -> 1 as alpha -> infinity, so H_coth predicts kappa(A) -> 1 for large A: the missing factor should VANISH in heavy nuclei. The present data (A <= 13) plateaus near 2.1-2.3 rather than trending to 1, so either alpha(A) itself saturates in this range or H_coth is incomplete. Extending the kappa(A) table to heavier mirror pairs is the sharp falsification test and needs no new theory.
data.honest_caveats: (1) Four data points, one free scale -- this cannot confirm anything; it can only fail. (2) arccoth is compressive on this range, so variance reduction is partly automatic; that is precisely why null transforms are scored alongside. (3) A^(1/3) was fixed in advance as the standard nuclear radius law, not selected post hoc. (4) Nothing is wired, and no kappa value is reproduced from theory -- the invariant remains open.
